scope: Corollary 4.11 (Random and signed sources) of the manuscript “Buffered comparison and stopping-band resolution in critical Ising” (preprints/Buffered-comparison-and-stopping-band-resolution-in-critical-Ising-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d5167e3fe5fb85f4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 18. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The conclusions of Proposition 4.2 hold after averaging over any ordered coupling of two random source configurations, with the appropriate common Gibbs continuation given each source. In particular, let µ be a Gibbs law with common pins and let q = q(σS) be an order-positive centered density for its source marginal. Then |Eµ[qh]| ≤ C∥h∥∞(w/s)−7/8+δ Eµ[qMJ ]. (4.20) The constants do not depend on the mass of the positive part of q.
